description: Check that a US bank routing number (ABA routing transit number, 9 digits) is well formed before you set up an ACH payment, a wire or a direct deposit. Send the routing number only, never an account number. Get back whether the check digit is right (3-7-1 weights), what the first two digits mean (Federal Reserve district, thrift, electronic-only, US Government or traveler's checks, or a range that is not assigned), the Federal Reserve district, and the check digit the first eight digits call for. A well-formed number can still be one no bank uses: this checks the form, not the bank. Answer fields: ok, verdict, result, rule, does_not, sources, observation, signature, verify. Errors: ok false with the reason (bad input, too large, hourly limit). Free. No model, no network, nothing you send is stored by the tool, and every answer is signed with LLPRO's key (check it at https://llpro.ai/aba-routing-check). Not legal, tax or financial advice.

routing_number.description: The 9-digit routing number, as text so a leading zero is kept (for example '021000021'). The routing number only: never send an account number.
